summary: Completed frontend-only validation on public preview URL for demo channels/scenario continuity/simulations, motion modes, responsiveness (768 + 320), and homepage regression paths.

integration_issues.issue: Console repeatedly logs browser warning: iframe uses sandbox with both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin, which can weaken sandbox isolation.

action_items: Review iframe sandbox policy tradeoff (allow-scripts + allow-same-origin) and tighten if product behavior allows.
Optional: reduce expected net::ERR_ABORTED console noise from interrupted asset loads during rapid route changes.
critical_code_review_comments: Demo iframe currently combines allow-scripts and allow-same-origin in sandbox; this triggers browser security warnings and reduces isolation guarantees.
No malformed HTML/SVG parse errors were observed in this run; previous malformed path issue appears resolved.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated all 8 channels switch correctly and all 72 channel-tab combinations show scenario-specific content. Verified tab labels preserved (case-insensitive text match), mock label visible, fullscreen preserves scenario query, iframe internal links/onclick continuity retain scenario param, play run adds autoplay=1 and advances tabs, pause works, and simulate step completes. Reduced-motion manual + prefers-reduced-motion both suppress scenario animation (scenario-trace animation none|0s). 768 and 320 checks show no horizontal overflow or clipping. Homepage regression checks (demo nav, waitlist modal open/close, resources route, newsletter input) passed.
rca of the issue: RCA-1 (console warning): Reproducible across demo tabs; browser warns because sandboxed iframe includes both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin, enabling stronger iframe capabilities than strict sandboxing. Mitigation: remove allow-same-origin if feasible, or document this as an accepted risk if same-origin scripting is required for scenario runtime. RCA-2 (non-blocking abort logs): During route transitions/reloads, in-flight asset/script requests are canceled by navigation, producing net::ERR_ABORTED lines; behavior is timing-related and not a functional failure.
